title: mapper: lambda forms, block params, by-name arguments, and EK9100 through the forms resolver (M3, part 1)
body:
Form resolution (rule 3, L1) through the forms resolver, which the
projector reads through its formResolver interface (lambdas.go):

- A lambda, an arrow, a function expression, or a method of an object
  literal, takes the resolver's form: plain as written; the Effect
  function form, its body as a generator; the program form, the lambda
  becomes its generator; and the dual form, $dual(program), which the
  prelude types Effect<A, E, R> & (() => Effect<A, E, R>). A dual that no
  call takes is a function value and takes the Effect function form, as
  the fork types it: returned or bound, it reads () => Effect<A, E, R>.
- Block params (D188): appended, f(args, block), or applied to the call,
  f(args)(block), which is also where a data-first dual's block goes,
  since f(block, args) and f(args)(block) are one call of a dual.
- By-name arguments (D147): in an Effect body, an argument the callee
  takes as a program becomes one instead of running where it stands. A
  name or a member at a position that takes only a program goes through
  $asProgram, which runs a function value as its program (D7).
- EK9100: where the rules cannot decide (Decision.Choice), the projector
  reports the resolver's Choice.Message() at the lambda or block and
  lowers the default's guess.

Also:
- A fork in a block goes through $scoped: the block's Scope owns the
  fiber, so Scope leaves R (D19, D96); a fork that is a lambda's
  expression body keeps it. The runtime's fork imported by name counts.
- A zero-argument call of a member of an effect module, such as
  Effect.currentSpan(), goes through $value, which runs an Effect value
  (D90); a namespace's members are never methods.
- A do expression's completion value, which the parser returns without a
  return keyword in the source, gets one (D187), boxed in a region.
- A region statement that ends its Effect function's own body lets its
  blocks fall off their ends and returns its completion unconditionally,
  so undefined joins A exactly where TypeScript finds an end reachable,
  an exhaustive switch included.
- The prelude's $gen joins the yielded Effects' E and R member by member:
  Effect.gen's own [Eff] extends [Effect<…, infer E, …>] merges them with
  subtype reduction, so an error that structurally extends another (a
  TaggedError with a name field against a { id, name } type) vanished.

New edit kinds: dual, scoped, program value.

Parity, concrete: 879 -> 1054 identical of 1243. Six declarations that
were identical are not: four negative cases (.fail) whose fork
declarations are unknown because the fork reports an error, and two
[Symbol.dispose] methods that the resolver gives the dual form.

title: mapper: a region's returns keep the enclosing function's literal types
body:
A return in a region's block now returns $box(value), its value joined
with a brand (prelude.d.ts), instead of the bare value. The block's
generator then never infers a single literal type, so it never widens
one on its own; $returned and $unboxed remove the brand where the
enclosing function returns the completion, and that function's return
inference sees every return site at once and widens as TypeScript does
for the source. handle-tail-resume three now gives the fork's
"no" | "stopped" | "yes" where the clause's own generator gave string.

A literal-preserving generator (a return type parameter constrained to
every type) fixed three but broke three others: the constraint also makes
the contextual type literal, so a template literal in a return typed as a
template literal type (decl-error describe and main) and a single literal
return in a region stayed a literal (handle-tail-resume main).

A completion passed on to an enclosing region after narrowing is boxed
again. Returns the parser writes, such as the arms of a returned match,
stay unboxed until match is lowered. The executable rendering now panics
with 'exec: kind X not implemented' for every kind but witness.

body:
packages/converter-worker runs effeck --noEmit --pretty false on one
file in a fresh temp dir beside a fixed project pinned to effeck 0.0.1,
effeck-runtime 0.0.1 and effect 4.0.5, and returns the exit code,

compile, diagnostics, the 8 KiB refusal, the timeout, the output

title: mapper: completion records across regions, try/catch/finally, provide, and handle (M2, part 1)
body:
The lowering plan's edits now carry a semantic kind (plan.go), and each
rendering maps kinds to text: syntax, witness, run, effect body,
contract, program, fail, service call, value call, region, record, and
dispatch. Helpers are written as references that the rendering resolves,
so the plan holds no checking-only text. The executable rendering is a
placeholder: it drops witnesses and otherwise writes the checking text.

Regions (regions.go), as the fork lowers them: a block of an Effect
function that a runtime helper wraps runs as a generator of its own, and
a return, break, or continue that leaves it completes the region, which
the statement after it dispatches on: it takes the jump, or passes the
completion on when the jump leaves an enclosing region too.

- try/catch/finally in an Effect body: $catch and $finally over the
  blocks' generators. Typed and Cause catch clauses are not lowered yet.
- provide blocks (D172): Effect.provide(Layers)(program), which keeps the
  source order; several providers become an array, and Key = value the
  layer $provideService(Key, "Key", value) (D173).
- handle statements (D132): the runtime's handle, one call per control,
  each clause '(params, $k) => generator'; the parser's continuation goes
  to resume, resumeWith, and abandon, and a tail resume returns
  $tailResume (D18).
- In the checking rendering a region's returns stay as written, so their
  values keep TypeScript's own return inference: the runtime's
  { kind, value } record would widen an inferred literal union through
  its property. A normal end returns the prelude's $end, a break or
  continue $jump(kind), and $returned and $jumped narrow the completion.
- A function declaration or method without an annotation that returns no
  value keeps A void when every path throws, as TypeScript infers for the
  source: its throws project to 'return (yield* $fail(x)) as void'.

clean file remains: handle-tail-resume three, where a clause's single
literal return widens in its own generator (the fork keeps the union
"no" | "stopped" | "yes").

title: lsp: hovers on Effeck forms' words no longer panic
body:
In an .effeck file, getTokenAtPosition found two kinds of source tokens
where TypeScript code has only trivia, and panicked ("did not expect
KindClassDeclaration to have KindIdentifier in its trivia"). 388 of about
